bull.t: Very strong cash generation and margins
bull.b: Sustained, large operating and free cash flows plus exceptionally high TTM margins give Micron durable financial flexibility to fund R&D, fabs and dividends. This level of cash generation supports multi-year capex cycles and strategic investments despite cyclical swings in the memory market.

A low leverage profile and large cash reserves materially increase Micron's resilience to down-cycles, support aggressive capital programs, and permit shareholder returns. Strong credit profile and reduced debt provide lasting optionality through multi-year fabs and technology transitions.

bull.t: Large strategic customer agreements (SCAs) and RPO visibility
bull.b: Material contracted volume and multi‑year RPO provide structural revenue visibility and demand anchoring across cycles. Customer commitments and deposits help de-risk utilization planning, inform capacity investments, and strengthen long-term OEM/hyperscaler partnerships.

bear.b: Memory markets historically oscillate; extreme recent margins reflect an upcycle that can reverse. Structural demand shifts, pricing normalization or oversupply would quickly compress profitability, making current profit levels potentially transient over a 2–6 month horizon and beyond.

bear.t: Very high and rising capital and operating spending
bear.b: Sustained multi-year capital intensity raises fixed costs and execution risk. Ongoing high CapEx and rising OpEx will pressure free cash flow variability, require disciplined returns on new capacity, and extend the time before incremental fabs contribute positively to per-bit economics.

bear.t: Persistent supply constraints and rising cost-per-bit
bear.b: Extended supply bottlenecks and slower bit growth amid tougher process nodes increase unit costs and limit industry's ability to meet demand. Higher cost-per-bit and complex ramps can compress long-term margins and slow share gains, challenging sustainable profitability over multi-year cycles.
